Layers menu · Direction A · 2026-10-21

Layers, by question

The sheet is grouped by what the reader is asking, not by what the data is. Each question has one primary choice (a tile row, the app's OptionRow) and its overlays as quiet switches below it. The questions a view does not answer collapse to one link row. Every row is drawn from one layer registry entry, so a new layer is one entry and no redesign. Drawn in the app's own tokens (themes/light.json, dark.json) and faces (Bricolage Grotesque, Archivo), on the square, ink-ruled Sheet. Phone width 390 × 844; light and dark side by side.

Where can I fish?Regulations on the day (streams and lakes). Overlays: private land, your spots. Parks, reserves and no-access are always on.
What is the water doing?Flow, level, temperature (Conditions). Overlays: gauges, flow arrows. On the Map tab it is one link row.
What is it like?Lakes: Stocked, Depth (instead of regulations). Ground: drawn map, satellite, downloaded corridors. Overlays: pools and runs, relief.
  • What leaves the sheet: the Streams paragraph (it controlled nothing), the Live data rows and the six attribution lines (to the menu's Sources and credits).
  • What stays, demoted: Palette, under a DISPLAY rule marked WHOLE APP — it is a setting, not a layer.
  • One colouring pathway: every choice writes mapModes inputs only (sets in the registry); colouring.ts paints.

1 · Default, Map tab

  • Three questions, in the order a reader asks them on this tab. Each has one primary choice (a tile, as today's OptionRow) and quiet secondary switches.
  • Where can I fish? is the default answer and now says so: the regulation colouring is a choice with its legend inside the tile (three lines that wrap, so the 613 px strip overflow is gone). 'Plain' is retired.
  • Private land finally has a switch (group ownership, default off). Parks / reserves / no-access are one fine line, not a switch: safety layers are not toggleable.
  • What is the water doing? lives on Conditions, so here it is one link row, not a paragraph. The count moves to the question.
  • Live data rows and the six attribution lines leave the sheet for the menu's Sources and credits; Palette stays, below a DISPLAY rule, marked WHOLE APP.
  • The sheet is the scroll Sheet with its body capped near 470 px (not a 520 px ScrollView inside a fixed sheet): no dead space, and over a third of the map stays visible above with the rail.

2 · On the Conditions map

  • The same sheet, ordered by this map's question. Only entries whose views include conditions draw: no Lakes tiles, no regulation tile.
  • Flow / Level / Temperature are the stream colour modes (one slot, the same mapModes input the legend writes). Gauges and Flow arrows become visible switches; both default on.
  • The Layers button now shows on Conditions (it sits on the rail), so 'basemap leaks with no control' is answered: the ground is chosen here too.
  • The question that belongs to the other tab collapses to a link row, symmetric with state 1.
  • Owner question: keep the quantity chips on the legend as well (two doors to one input), or move them here only?

3 · Stocked / Depth prepared, not fed

  • Owner rule (decisions.md, 2026-10-21): the toggles exist, are greyed, and say NO DATA YET. The swatches dim but keep their ramp, so the reader still sees what is coming.
  • One fine line gives the reason and the promise: they switch on by themselves. Availability is derived from the release (needs.release), never set by hand.
  • LAKES is labelled INSTEAD OF REGULATIONS: Stocked and Depth share the lake slot with the regulation tile. Picking one leaves streams on regulations and the regulation tile says 'Streams only — lakes show Stocked' (see the fed sample below).
  • Depth = lake mode surveyed + group depth in one entry: one tile, two mapModes inputs.

4 · Satellite while offline

  • Satellite (Esri World Imagery) is needs.network: offline it greys with NEEDS A CONNECTION and the drawn map shows.
  • A reader who chose satellite keeps that choice: the tile carries a dashed accent frame (chosen, waiting) and the drawn map tile says SHOWING. Back online, satellite returns without a tap.
  • The closed map says so too: a quiet chip top-left, 'Offline · drawn map'. Every non-default layer gets a chip like this, so the closed map always shows its state.
  • Online, the tile reads ONLINE ONLY as a hint, before anyone is surprised in a canyon.

5 · Future layers slot in

  • Outlined in magenta (mockup only): four new registry entries (Your spots sits higher in the same sheet, sample below), no new component and no new section.
  • Corridors (downloaded stream imagery) is one more base entry in the ground slot: a third tile, with its count as the note.
  • Pools and runs and Relief are overlay entries with needs.built: false, so they draw as COMING SOON rows until they ship.
  • Your spots (the Spots lane) is an overlay under Where can I fish?, if the owner decides spots draw as a layer.
  • The rail's Layers button carries a count of non-default layers (2), and each shows as a chip on the closed map.

The layer registry this design implies

One table drives the sheet, the rail badge, the closed-map chips and the accessible names. question picks the section, slot makes a radio (tiles) and no slot makes a switch, views decides where it draws, and needs derives availability (ok · no-data · online-only · coming-soon) with its reason words from @app/core.

// @app/core/src/layers.ts — THE LAYER REGISTRY. One entry per thing the Layers sheet can show.
// The sheet, the rail badge, the map chips and the a11y names all read this; adding a layer is one entry
// plus its words. An entry changes ONLY mapModes inputs: colouring.ts (via applyLook) does the painting.

export type LayerKind = "base" | "colour-mode" | "overlay" | "setting";
export type Question  = "where" | "doing" | "like" | "display";
export type ViewId    = "map" | "water" | "conditions" | "search";
/** Radio slots: entries sharing a slot replace one another. Overlays have no slot (each is its own switch). */
export type Slot      = "stream-colour" | "lake-colour" | "ground" | "palette";

export interface LayerEntry {
  id: string;
  question: Question;              // which section it draws under
  kind: LayerKind;
  slot?: Slot | readonly Slot[];   // regulations fills two slots (streams AND lakes)
  views: readonly ViewId[];        // the maps it applies to; elsewhere it is not drawn at all
  default: boolean | Partial<Record<ViewId, boolean>>;
  /** what choosing it sets — mapModes inputs only, never a colour */
  sets: {
    modes?: Partial<Record<"stream" | "lake", string>>;  // colour modes in the style
    groups?: readonly string[];                          // toggleable style groups (depth, ownership…)
    runtime?: string;                                    // a runtime layer (gauges, spots)
    basemap?: "drawn" | "satellite" | "corridors";
    theme?: ThemeName;
  };
  /** what must be true for it to work; availability is DERIVED from this, never set by hand */
  needs?: {
    release?: string;     // a value the release must carry ("lake.stocked")   -> no-data
    network?: true;       // streamed, online only                              -> online-only
    download?: string;    // a pack the reader must have downloaded             -> no-data ("none downloaded")
    built?: false;        // declared before it ships                           -> coming-soon
  };
  swatch: readonly [TokenRef, TokenRef, TokenRef];  // style tokens, never hexes
  count?: CountKey;        // source.counts() key for the tile note / question note
  words: LayerWordsKey;    // LAYER_WORDS in @app/core: title, detail, legend, and one reason per availability
}

export type Availability =
  | { state: "ok" }
  | { state: "no-data";     reason: string }   // "NO DATA YET" — switches on by itself
  | { state: "online-only"; reason: string }   // "NEEDS A CONNECTION" — choice is kept
  | { state: "coming-soon"; reason: string };  // "COMING SOON"

export function availability(e: LayerEntry, ctx: { carries(k: string): boolean; online: boolean; downloaded(k: string): number }): Availability {
  const w = LAYER_WORDS[e.words];
  if (e.needs?.built === false)                        return { state: "coming-soon", reason: w.soon ?? LAYER_REASON.soon };
  if (e.needs?.release && !ctx.carries(e.needs.release)) return { state: "no-data",   reason: LAYER_REASON.noData };
  if (e.needs?.download && !ctx.downloaded(e.needs.download)) return { state: "no-data", reason: LAYER_REASON.noneDownloaded };
  if (e.needs?.network && !ctx.online)                 return { state: "online-only", reason: LAYER_REASON.offline };
  return { state: "ok" };
}

/** Questions: their order per view, and the view that owns them (elsewhere they collapse to a link row). */
export const QUESTIONS: Record<Question, { home?: ViewId; order: Partial<Record<ViewId, number>> }> = {
  where:   { home: "map",        order: { map: 0, water: 0, search: 0, conditions: 2 } },
  doing:   { home: "conditions", order: { conditions: 0, map: 1, water: 1, search: 1 } },
  like:    {                     order: { map: 2, water: 2, search: 2, conditions: 1 } },
  display: {                     order: { map: 9, water: 9, search: 9, conditions: 9 } },
};

const BROWSE: ViewId[] = ["map", "water", "search"];
const ALL: ViewId[]    = ["map", "water", "search", "conditions"];
